description: This course explores the Earth's oceans in terms of geological, chemical, physical, and biological oceanography, with emphasis on understanding the oceans as an integrated system. We also discuss the ocean's role in mitigating global change and the consequences for oceanic ecosystems and human society.

title: How the Earth Works: The Water Cycle and Environment
description: This course describes behavior of earth materials in the surficial environment. Water is the main transport agent in the geological cycle; its unique properties and exchange rates among oceans, lakes, rivers, and groundwater are one focus. Interaction between water reservoirs and physical and chemical weathering of soils, sediments, and rocks also are discussed. Impact of humans on the surficial environment is a unifying theme because we can affect hydrologic and geochemical cycles.

title: OUR DYNAMIC PLANET
description: Our Dynamic Planet is an introduction to the various earth sciences that constitute the earth’s physical environment. They include cartography, geology, geomorphology, hydrology, meteorology and climatology. Specific topics include: a) maps, b) rocks, c) continental drift, d) volcanoes, e) erosion, f) caves and karst landscapes, g) streams, h) glaciers, i) landforms, j) weather, k) precipitation, l) wind, m) storms, and n) climate. The course also covers environmental hazards, such as, earthquakes, tsunamis, landslides, sinkhole flooding and collapses, volcano eruptions, tornadoes, hurricanes, floods and climate change.

title: General Biology II
description: Biology 1040 is the second course of a twosemester sequence in general biology that follows Biology 1030 (General Biology I). This course is intended for both Biology majors and non-majors that require a solid introduction to the science of biology. It provides an evolutionary approach to the study of living systems and emphasizes the basic structure and function of animals, especially humans and plants. Topics include the various tissues and organ systems that make up the animal and plant bodies; regulation of growth, development and reproduction; an introduction to the diversity of living organisms; the evolution and diversity of plants; and an introduction to ecology.

title: Physical Geography
description: Geography is a very broad discipline that is generally divided into two major sub-disciplines: human geography and physical geography. Physical geography focuses on topics such as: the formation and evolution of landforms, atmospheric and oceanic circulation, climate and weather, natural resources, ecosystems, and the interaction between humans and their physical environment. In this course we will focus on four major areas: The Energy and Atmosphere System; Water, Weather, & Climate Systems; The Geosphere: Earth’s Interior & Surface; The Biosphere.

title: Physical Geology
description: This course provides an understanding of the interacting physical geological principles and processes that shape the Earth. We will explore some fundamental principles related to geologic processes that shape the surface of the Earth, plate tectonics, planetary resources, geologic hazards, and Earth’s interior processes. Basic geological principles are applied to understanding our planet and the processes that bring about change. We will review the causes and effects of natural disasters, climate change, and planetary resources that we use.
